To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the positively charged cyclodextins (CD) derivatives, octakis[6(2-aminoethyl thio)-6-deoxi]-γ-CDs (γCys), are able to bind oxacillin (OXA) in aqueous solution with high binding constants, in an enthalpic and entropic favorable process and are able to reduce the rate of OXA hydrolysis by the oxa-1 beta lactamase.

the most efficient host for delivery of oxacilline to mammalian cells was the positively charged γCys that forms the strongest complex with the penicillin in an enthalpic and entropic favorable process and that reduces 2.4 fold the rate of hydrolysation of oxacillin by oxa-1 beta lactamase.

Designed, protonated, positively charged, octakis[6-deoxy-6-(2-ammoniopropanoic acid) thio]-β- and - γ-CDs form strong inclusion complexes with penicillins and offer protection against β- lactamase-induced hydroysis."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a CD-based carrier that can protect penicillin antibiotics from enzymatic degradation and deliver them across the cell membrane.
the design and synthesis of novel CD derivatives with the potential to act as efficient carriers for the protection and delivery of antibiotics.
the development of cyclodextrin derivatives as carriers for the intracellular delivery of antibiotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
positively charged CDs with enhanced binding of antibiotics are a promising tool for the delivery of penicillin derivatives to mammalian cells.

the most suitable CD for the delivery of penicillin antibiotics should be the one that is able to: (1) present a sufficiently elongated cavity space, (2) be positively charged at physiological pH and (3) form strong complexes with the antibiotics in aqueous solution.
the positively charged cyclodextins, especially those with elongated cavity, are the optimal candidates for the protection and the intracellular delivery of oxacillins and other penicillins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cationic CD host, with enhanced cavity space and positively charged, can form a strong complex with an antibiotic, in an enthalpic and entropic driven process.
positively charged CDs with enhanced binding affinity of penicillns can be considered as promising vehicles for protection and delivery.

the positively charged γCys derivative is the optimal host for delivery of oxacil- lins to mammalian macrophages and other cells that will also protect them against β-lacta- mase-induced hydrolytic inactivation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of CD hosts with enhanced binding affinity for penicillins is possible and that these can offer protection against enzymatic hydrolysis and can also facilitate cell entry and intracellular uptake.

the design of positively charged CD hosts can be an effective strategy to improve the complexation of penicillines and to reduce β-lactam hydrolysis by β-lactamases, while maintaining the cell crossing and internalization capabilities of these drugs.
the use of positively charged cyclodextins can enhance the binding of aminopenicillin derivatives and that this can lead to a better protection against β-lacatamase hydrolysis.
